correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, deleting marker 1 gives one of n-1 singleton-2 outputs, so no code can exceed n-1. At equality both singleton-output position maps are permutations. Each ordered pair of singleton-output positions determines exactly one source word unless the positions coincide, when it determines two possible marker orientations. Explicit before/between/after zero-deletion pairs prove that two different permutation rows conflict exactly when both the row and column rise by one with equal orientation. Alternating orientations on the identity permutation attain n-1 at all lengths. The count B_k sums 2 choices per run of consecutive fixed points over permutations with no rising succession off the diagonal; the subset DP counts exactly these assignments. Direct deletion-set comparisons for all signed permutations k<=8, brute-force maximum codebooks n=2..6 and DP k<=11 agree. Finite checking is not the proof of the all-length claim.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of every optimum one-deletion-correcting code at a fixed ternary composition and an exact all-length count of their labeled codebooks. The elementary size bound alone would be too routine, but the signed permutation bijection, local collision lemma, and subset DP capture the full optimizer space. This structural space is relevant to choosing a capacity-optimal code with supplementary properties; no downstream theorem or broader-alphabet formula is claimed.
